# Koin Compiler Plugin — Kotlin Compiler Plugin for Koin DI

> Native Kotlin Compiler Plugin (K2) for the Koin dependency injection framework. Compiles both Koin styles — Koin DSL (Compiler Plugin DSL `single<T>()`, ...) and Koin Annotations (`@Singleton`, `@Factory`, `@KoinViewModel`, ...) — and checks the whole dependency graph at build time. Compile safe in both styles: no KSP, no kapt, no generated files.

## Key Facts

- **Version**: 1.2.1
- **Language**: Kotlin, K2 compiler required — Kotlin 2.3.20 minimum; verified 2.3.20, 2.4.0, 2.4.10, 2.4.20 (`supported-kotlin-versions.txt`)
- **Koin compatibility**: Koin 4.2.0+ — use the latest Koin BOM (4.2.2)
- **Replaces**: the Koin KSP processor (`koin-ksp-compiler`), now deprecated
- **License**: Apache 2.0
- **Repository**: https://github.com/InsertKoinIO/koin-compiler-plugin
- **Parent project (Koin)**: https://github.com/InsertKoinIO/koin

## Koin in short

- **Two styles, one container** — **Koin DSL** (`module { }`, Compiler Plugin DSL `single<T>()`) or **Koin Annotations** (`@Singleton`, `@Factory`, `@KoinViewModel`), the same model as Hilt / Dagger and **JSR-330 compatible** (`@Inject`, `@Singleton`, `@Named`, `@Qualifier` from `javax.inject` / `jakarta.inject`).
- **Choose one style explicitly** per project and keep to it. Don't mix Annotations and DSL unless asked — and then one style per module, never both inside a module.
- **DSL keeps DI out of the code** — classes carry no DI annotations; wiring lives in separate `module { }` files.
- **Compile safe in both styles** — this plugin checks the whole graph at build time, DSL and Annotations alike. Replaces runtime `verify()` / `checkModules()`.
- **Smart configuration** — `@Configuration` and `@ComponentScan` discover modules and components across Gradle modules. DSL apps assemble modules with `includes(...)`.
- **Kotlin Multiplatform** — Android, iOS, desktop, web and server (Ktor), one plugin, no per-target configuration.
- **Runtime** — app behavior, performance and memory with Kotzilla (see "AI agents" below).

## Installation

```kotlin
// settings.gradle.kts — Gradle Plugin Portal is enabled by default
// Or add: pluginManagement { repositories { gradlePluginPortal() } }

// build.gradle.kts (per-module, in any module that defines or starts Koin)
plugins {
    id("io.insert-koin.compiler.plugin") version "1.2.1"
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform("io.insert-koin:koin-bom:4.2.2"))   // versions every Koin artifact
    implementation("io.insert-koin:koin-core")
    // Annotations style (or Compiler Plugin DSL classes carrying @Named / @InjectedParam / @Qualifier):
    implementation("io.insert-koin:koin-annotations")           // version from the BOM
}
```

Never add KSP for Koin: no `com.google.devtools.ksp`, no `koin-ksp-compiler`, no `io.insert-koin:koin-annotations:2.x` pin (the KSP artifact), no `org.koin.ksp.generated.*` imports.

## Plugin Configuration

```kotlin
koinCompiler {
    userLogs = true            // Log discovered components (default: false)
    debugLogs = false          // Verbose internal processing logs
    unsafeDslChecks = true     // Validate create(::T) is the only call in scope { ... } lambdas
    skipDefaultValues = true   // Skip injection for params with Kotlin default values (non-null, unannotated)
    compileSafety = true       // Compile-time dependency graph validation (A3/A4) — keep it on
    strictSafety = null        // null = auto-detect; true forces it on
}
```

### Compile Safety Levels

When `compileSafety = true` (default), the plugin validates the dependency graph:

- **A3 — Full Graph**: at the Koin entry point (`startKoin<T>()` / `@KoinApplication`, or classic `startKoin { modules(...) }` for DSL apps), validates every reachable definition
- **A4 — Call-Site**: every `get<T>()`, `inject<T>()`, `koinViewModel<T>()`, etc. must resolve to a known definition

Since 1.1.0 there is no per-module pass: a module without a Koin entry point is verified where the app assembles the graph. Works with both the DSL and annotation styles. Replaces runtime `verify()` / `checkModules()`. Errors are reported as `[KOIN-…]` diagnostics.

### Strict Safety (Incremental Compilation Bypass)

Auto-enabled on modules containing `startKoin`, `koinApplication`, or `@KoinApplication`. Forces the entry point's `compileKotlin` to re-run every build so full-graph (A3) validation isn't skipped by Kotlin's incremental compiler when DSL lambda bodies or `@ComponentScan` packages change. Once detected, `strictSafety = false` is ignored; use `strictSafetyForceOff = true` only for a detector misfire. No effect when `compileSafety = false`.

## Koin DSL — three forms

All three are compiled and compile-time checked by the plugin (since 1.2.x, including `singleOf(::T)` and `get()` calls inside lambdas).

| Form | Example | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| **Compiler Plugin DSL** | `single<MyClass>()`, `single { create(::MyClass) }` | **Recommended with the Compiler Plugin** — plain constructor or function builder |
| Constructor DSL | `singleOf(::MyClass)` | Project without the Compiler Plugin, or matching existing code |
| Classic DSL | `single { MyClass(get()) }` | A custom expression a constructor or function builder can't express |

Compiler Plugin DSL primitives and the reified entry points import from **`org.koin.plugin.module.dsl`**. The Constructor DSL `*Of` family lives in `org.koin.core.module.dsl`.

### Compiler Plugin DSL functions

| Function | Receiver | Generates |
|---|---|---|
| `single<T>()` | `Module` | Singleton from primary constructor |
| `factory<T>()` | `Module` | Factory from primary constructor |
| `viewModel<T>()` | `Module` | ViewModel from primary constructor |
| `worker<T>()` | `Module` | WorkManager Worker from primary constructor |
| `scoped<T>()` | `ScopeDSL` | Scoped from primary constructor |
| `create(::T)` | `Scope` | Constructor or function-builder reference inside a definition lambda |
| `module<T>()` | `KoinApplication` | Loads a single `@Module` class (Annotations escape hatch) |
| `modules(vararg KClass)` | `KoinApplication` | Loads multiple `@Module` classes |
| `startKoin<T>()` | top-level | `@KoinApplication` entry point — triggers discovery and full-graph (A3) validation |
| `koinApplication<T>()` | top-level | Same as `startKoin<T>()` but returns the `KoinApplication` |
| `koinConfiguration<T>()` | top-level | KMP-friendly Koin configuration |

### Example

```kotlin
import org.koin.core.context.startKoin
import org.koin.core.module.dsl.bind
import org.koin.dsl.module
import org.koin.plugin.module.dsl.*

val appModule = module {
    includes(dataModule)
    single<Database>()                                // singleton, auto-wired
    single<UserRepositoryImpl>().bind<UserRepository>()
    factory<GetUserUseCase>()                         // factory, auto-wired
    viewModel<HomeViewModel>()
    worker<SyncWorker>()
    single { create(::buildRetrofit) }                // function builder for third-party types

    scope<UserSession> {
        scoped<UserPreferences>()
    }
}

class MyApp : Application() {
    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        startKoin {                                   // DSL: classic startKoin, one app module
            androidContext(this@MyApp)
            modules(appModule)
        }
    }
}
```

## Annotations

JSR-330 compatible: `javax.inject` / `jakarta.inject` `@Inject`, `@Singleton`, `@Named`, `@Qualifier` work as-is. Koin annotations import from `org.koin.core.annotation.*`. Prefer `@Singleton` over `@Single`.

### Definition Annotations

Apply to classes, to functions inside `@Module` classes, or to top-level functions (discovered by `@ComponentScan`).

| Annotation | Generates |
|---|---|
| `@Singleton` / `@Single` | `single { }` |
| `@Factory` | `factory { }` |
| `@Scoped` | `scoped { }` |
| `@KoinViewModel` | `viewModel { }` |
| `@KoinWorker` | `worker { }` |

A `@Singleton` / `@Factory` class implementing a single interface is bound to it automatically.

### Module Annotations

| Annotation | Effect |
|---|---|
| `@Module` | Marks a class as a Koin module container |
| `@ComponentScan("pkg")` | Scans package(s) for annotated classes and top-level functions — keep it on the module's own package |
| `@Configuration` | Auto-discovered by `@KoinApplication` (supports labels: `@Configuration("test", "prod")`) |
| `@KoinApplication(modules)` | Application entry point — assembles `@Configuration` modules and runs full-graph validation |

Each Gradle module's root module carries `@Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("own.package")`. Missing one of the three means a runtime `NoDefinitionFoundException`, not a compile error. Load a module explicitly with `modules(module<AppModule>())`, never `AppModule().module`.

### Parameter Annotations

| Annotation | Effect |
|---|---|
| `@Named("x")` | String qualifier → `named("x")` |
| `@Qualifier(name = "x")` | String qualifier → `named("x")` |
| `@Qualifier(MyType::class)` | Type qualifier → `typeQualifier<MyType>()` |
| `@InjectedParam` | Uses `ParametersHolder.get()` |
| `@Property("key")` | Injects a property value (warns if no `@PropertyValue` default) |
| `@PropertyValue("key")` | Provides a default value for `@Property` |
| `@Provided` | Type is supplied externally — skipped during safety validation |
| `@ScopeId(name = "x")` | Resolves from a named scope → `getScope("x").get<T>()` |
| `@ScopeId(MyScope::class)` | Resolves from a typed scope |

### Example

```kotlin
import org.koin.core.annotation.*
import org.koin.plugin.module.dsl.startKoin

@Module
@Configuration
@ComponentScan("com.myapp")
class AppModule

@Singleton
class Database

@Singleton
class UserRepository(private val db: Database)

@KoinViewModel
class HomeViewModel(
    private val repo: UserRepository,
    @InjectedParam val userId: String,
) : ViewModel()

// Top-level provider functions are also discovered by @ComponentScan
@Singleton
fun provideJson(): Json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }

@KoinApplication
class MyApp : Application() {
    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        startKoin<MyApp> { androidContext(this@MyApp) }   // no modules(...) — discovered
    }
}
```

## Migration from KSP (Koin Annotations)

The compiler plugin replaces the deprecated KSP processor (`koin-ksp-compiler`). Annotations stay the same; remove the KSP setup and `org.koin.ksp.generated.*` imports, then apply the Kotlin compiler plugin. See: https://github.com/InsertKoinIO/koin-compiler-plugin/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION_FROM_KSP.md

## AI agents

- **Koin skills** (official, for Claude Code and other agents): set up Koin, write Koin code, migrate from Hilt, Dagger, Toothpick, Kodein, Koin KSP or Koin 3.x, diagnose Koin apps — https://github.com/InsertKoinIO/koin-skills. Install guide: https://insert-koin.io/docs/tooling/ai-agents. Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add InsertKoinIO/koin-skills`, then `/plugin install koin@koin-skills`. Other agents (Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini…): `npx skills add InsertKoinIO/koin-skills` (Node.js 22+)
- **Kotzilla MCP** — `https://mcp.kotzilla.io/mcp`: diagnose `[KOIN-…]` compile-safety errors and Koin runtime exceptions; with the Kotzilla SDK, debug app behavior, performance and memory. The plugin checks the graph is complete; Kotzilla checks how it behaves. Claude Code: `claude mcp add kotzilla --transport http https://mcp.kotzilla.io/mcp`
